Seasonal Timing

How does earlier warming or later cooling affect simulated demand?

This page compares when hot weather started and ended in each year from 2022 to 2026 with a typical year (1991–2020), for one province at a time, and then shows what that timing would mean in our simulated sales.

How to read this page: Select a province, season and year. The left card compares that year's seasonal timing with 1991–2020. The right card shows an illustrative synthetic sales scenario. Explore the charts below for historical comparisons and simulated demand.

Left: one observed year. Right: a hypothetical average over 2022–2026 from our simulation. They describe different things and should not be read as the same observation.

HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO

Read with care.
  • REAL WEATHER · ERA5 and HISTORICAL REFERENCE are observations used for every comparison with 1991–2020. Results are for one provincial-centre point, not for all of Türkiye.
  • REAL WEATHER · best_match is a different Open-Meteo dataset (up to about 2 °C apart on average in some provinces); it drives the synthetic sales and Pages 1–2, and is never mixed with ERA5 in one comparison.
  • SYNTHETIC SALES are simulated, not actual Arçelik or Beko sales; their link to temperature was built into the simulation.
  • HYPOTHETICAL SCENARIO results are not forecasts and not causal estimates.
  • Onset dates depend on the threshold rule (see Advanced analysis). Mersin's autumn threshold has lower reliability. 2026 data end on 31 Oct, so the same autumn cut-offs are used in every year.
Advanced analysis & methodology details

Sensitivity of the onset date to the rule

Each row is one rule. Dates are compared with the 1991–2020 median under the same rule. E / L = earlier / later than the middle half (interquartile range) of the reference years.

Method notes

    Data. Weather: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API and Forecast API (CC BY 4.0), daily maximum temperature at 2 m, one provincial-centre point per province, Europe/Istanbul time, ; Pages 1–2 and the synthetic sales use the default "best_match" dataset; Page 3 compares years with the 1991–2020 reference using ERA5 only. Forecast snapshot retrieved . Sales: synthetic, simulated with a fixed seed (449) to show the workflow; they are not actual Arçelik or Beko sales, and the temperature–sales link is built into the simulation, not discovered.

    Rules. Heat-wave day: Tmax ≥ 35 °C on at least 3 consecutive days (per province). Hot week: Mon–Sun mean Tmax ≥ 30 °C; the hot-week uplift compares hot and normal complete weeks within May–September only (descriptive, not causal). Forecast alert: any of the next 7 forecast days with Tmax > 35 °C. Descriptive analytics only: no forecasting models, machine learning or optimisation.
